sections.label: Modest economic growth
sections.summary: The economy grew by a modest 1.1%, avoiding a recession.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our economy grew by a modest 1.1%, avoiding a recession.

sections.label: GDP growth forecast
sections.summary: Besides lower inflation, GDP growth is expected at 1.0% to 3.0%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Besides lower inflation, we expect higher gross domestic product (GDP) growth at 1.0% to 3.0%.

sections.label: Cost-of-Living Support Package
sections.summary: Early indicators of a negative trend led to the Cost-of-Living Support Package and an enhanced Assurance Package over $10 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We had picked up early indicators of this negative trend.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And that is why I introduced the Cost-of-Living Support Package in September last year and enhanced the Assurance Package to over $10 billion.

sections.label: CDC Vouchers and cash payment
sections.summary: An additional $600 in CDC Vouchers for all Singaporean households and a Cost-of-Living Special Payment of $200 to $400 in cash.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, I will provide an additional $600 in Community Development Council (CDC) Vouchers for all Singaporean households.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Second, I will provide a Cost-of-Living Special Payment of between $200 and $400 in cash.

sections.label: HDB U-Save rebates
sections.summary: Eligible HDB households can receive two-and-a-half times regular U-Save rebates, or up to $950, in FY2024.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In total, eligible HDB households can expect to receive two-and-a-half times the amount of regular U-Save rebates, or up to $950, in FY2024.

sections.label: Assurance Package cost
sections.summary: The additional support under the Assurance Package will cost $1.9 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Altogether, the additional support under the Assurance Package will cost $1.9 billion.

sections.label: Lower-income household benefits
sections.summary: A lower-income household of four with two young children will receive about $5,500 in benefits in FY2024.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: A lower-income household of four, with two young children, will receive about $5,500 in benefits in FY2024.

sections.label: GST Voucher Fund top-up
sections.summary: The speaker will top up the GST Voucher Fund by $6 billion beyond the Assurance Package.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Beyond the Assurance Package, I will top up the Good and Services Tax (GST) Voucher Fund by $6 billion.

sections.label: Enterprise Support Package
sections.summary: An Enterprise Support Package will provide $1.3 billion, including a 50% Corporate Income Tax Rebate capped at $40,000 in Year of Assessment 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Many companies have seen increases in their wage bills, rental, and utilities, amongst others.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will therefore introduce an Enterprise Support Package, which will provide $1.3 billion in support to companies.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, companies will receive a 50% Corporate Income Tax Rebate, capped at $40,000, in the Year of Assessment 2024.

sections.label: Refundable Investment Credit and fund top-up
sections.summary: A new Refundable Investment Credit will be introduced, and the National Productivity Fund topped up by $2 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But neither should we stand still and just do nothing.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will therefore enhance our investment promotion toolkit by introducing a new Refundable Investment Credit.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is a tax credit with a refundable cash feature.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It will support high-value and substantive economic activities, including the setting up or expansion of manufacturing facilities; new innovation and R&D activities; as well as activities in support of the green transition.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To support this and other investment promotion efforts, I will top up the National Productivity Fund by $2 billion this year.

sections.label: Financial Sector Development Fund top-up
sections.summary: The speaker will top up the Financial Sector Development Fund by $2 billion to reinforce competitive lead.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, in this Budget, I will set aside resources to reinforce our competitive lead.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will top up the Financial Sector Development Fund by $2 billion.

sections.label: Additional RIE2025 investment
sections.summary: A further $3 billion will be invested in the RIE2025 plan, which was launched in 2020 with $25 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In 2020, we launched the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 (RIE2025) plan, with a commitment of $25 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will invest a further $3 billion in RIE2025.

sections.label: AI investment over five years
sections.summary: More than $1 billion will be invested over five years into AI compute, talent and industry development.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To support this strategy and further catalyse AI activities, I will invest more than $1 billion over the next five years into AI compute, talent and industry development.

sections.label: 10 Gbps broadband access
sections.summary: Additional investments aim to enable mass market access to broadband speeds of up to 10 Gigabits per second in the second half of this decade.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: With the additional investments, we aim to enable mass market access to broadband speeds of up to 10 Gigabits per second in the second half of this decade.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is 10 times faster than the broadband speed in most homes today.

sections.label: Enhancing PACT partnerships
sections.summary: PACT will be enhanced to support partnerships in more areas, including capability training, internationalisation and corporate venturing.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This supports collaborations between larger companies and SMEs, in the areas of supplier development and co-innovation.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will enhance PACT to support partnerships in more areas – including capability training, internationalisation and corporate venturing.

sections.label: Extending green loans support
sections.summary: Enhanced support for green loans under the Enterprise Financing Scheme will be extended and expanded to more sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In other words, to play in the MNE value chain, our own companies must be “sustainability-ready”.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will therefore extend the enhanced support for green loans under the Enterprise Financing Scheme, and expand its scope to help more of our SMEs adopt green solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This was introduced in 2022 for companies in the Food Services, Food Manufacturing and Retail sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will extend the grant to more sectors including Manufacturing, Construction, Maritime and Data Centres and their users.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit and training spending
sections.summary: Government spending on Continuing Education and Training nearly doubled to $0.9 billion, with $500 SkillsFuture Credit for every Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Since then, Government spending on Continuing Education and Training has nearly doubled to $0.9 billion last year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Today, every Singaporean gets a $500 SkillsFuture Credit, and all employers can get support to train their workers.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme
sections.summary: A new SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme will give Singaporeans aged 40 and above a $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit top-up.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But we know that taking time off from work to attend training courses over an extended period is not easy, especially for those in their 40s and 50s with financial and caregiving obligations.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will therefore introduce a new SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme to better support our mid-career workers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, I will give all Singaporeans aged 40 and above a top-up in SkillsFuture Credit of $4,000.

sections.label: Subsidies for older diploma study
sections.summary: Subsidies will be provided to Singaporeans aged 40 and above to pursue another full-time diploma from Academic Year 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Second, to provide more reskilling options, I will provide subsidies to all Singaporeans aged 40 and above to pursue another full-time diploma at our polytechnics, the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) and Arts Institutions from Academic Year 2025 onwards.

sections.label: Monthly training allowance for older learners
sections.summary: Singaporeans aged 40 and above in selected full-time courses get a monthly training allowance of 50% of average income, capped at $3,000.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Third, I will provide a monthly training allowance to Singaporeans aged 40 and above who enrol in selected full-time courses.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The training allowance will be equivalent to 50% of one’s average income over the latest available 12-month period and it will be capped at $3,000 per month.

sections.label: Support for involuntarily unemployed
sections.summary: A temporary financial support scheme will be introduced for the involuntarily unemployed while they undergo training or look for better-fitting jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In particular, we will introduce a temporary financial support scheme for the involuntarily unemployed, while they undergo training or look for better-fitting jobs.

sections.label: Enhanced Workfare Income Supplement
sections.summary: The Workfare Income Supplement qualifying income cap rises from $2,500 to $3,000, and maximum annual payout for lower-wage senior workers rises from $4,200 to $4,900.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, I will enhance the Workfare Income Supplement scheme from next year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will raise the qualifying income cap from $2,500 to $3,000.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Lower-wage senior workers will qualify for a maximum annual payout of $4,900, up from $4,200 today.

sections.label: Higher Local Qualifying Salary rates
sections.summary: The Local Qualifying Salary for full-time workers rises from $1,400 to $1,600, and the minimum hourly rate from $9 to $10.50.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The LQS for full-time workers will be raised from $1,400 to $1,600 from this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The minimum hourly rate will be increased from $9 to $10.50 per hour.

sections.label: Raised co-funding levels
sections.summary: The Government will raise co-funding levels this year from a maximum of 30% to a maximum of 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, the Government will do its part to help.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will raise the co-funding levels for this year, from a maximum of 30%, to a maximum of 50%.

sections.label: CPF top-up for diploma students
sections.summary: Students who attain diplomas will receive a further $10,000 top-up to their CPF Ordinary Accounts.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Second, when these students attain their diplomas, I will provide a further $10,000 top-up to their Central Provident Fund (CPF) Ordinary Accounts.

sections.label: Quarterly payouts for employed adults
sections.summary: Adults in the family can each receive payouts of up to $600 every quarter through cash and CPF if employed.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For example, adults in the family can each receive payouts of up to $600 every quarter, through a combination of cash and CPF, if they secure a job and stay employed.

sections.label: Lower preschool fee caps
sections.summary: Monthly childcare fee caps in Government-supported preschools will be reduced in 2025 to $640 for Anchor Operators and $680 for Partner Operators.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will lower the fees further so that full-day preschool expenses for dual-income families will be comparable to those of primary school and after-school student care.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will reduce monthly childcare fee caps in Government-supported preschools in 2025, to $640 for Anchor Operators and $680 for Partner Operators.

sections.label: Subsidies for lower-income families
sections.summary: Higher subsidies currently given to children with working mothers will be extended to all children from lower-income families, including those with non-working mothers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Currently, more subsidies are given to children with working mothers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will extend these higher subsidies to all children from lower-income families, including those with non-working mothers.

sections.label: Edusave awards and endowment top-up
sections.summary: The Edusave Endowment Fund will be topped up by $2 billion to support enhanced Edusave awards and other education initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We want to encourage and recognise students who demonstrate such competencies, including by enhancing the Edusave awards.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will therefore top up the Edusave Endowment Fund by $2 billion to support these and other education initiatives.

sections.label: PPHS voucher for renting families
sections.summary: A PPHS (Open Market) Voucher for one year will be provided to eligible families who rent a HDB flat in the open market.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But in the interim, we want to do more to support such young families with urgent housing needs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will therefore provide a PPHS (Open Market) Voucher for one year, to support eligible families who rent a HDB flat in the open market.

sections.label: SPED school maximum monthly fees
sections.summary: Maximum monthly fees at SPED schools will be reduced to $90 from $150.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As a first step, I will reduce the maximum monthly fees at SPED schools to $90, down from $150 today.

sections.label: CPF rates for senior workers
sections.summary: CPF contribution rates for those aged 55 to 65 will rise by 1.5 percentage points in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, in line with the recommendations of the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers, we will continue with the next step of planned CPF contribution rate increases for senior workers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will increase the CPF contribution rates for those aged 55 to 65 by a further 1.5 percentage points in 2025.

sections.label: Enhanced Retirement Sum increase
sections.summary: The ERS will rise from three to four times the Basic Retirement Sum from 2025, reaching $426,000.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The ERS is the maximum amount that members can put into their CPF Retirement Accounts to receive CPF payouts.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will increase the ERS from three times the Basic Retirement Sum, to four times from 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This means the ERS next year will be $426,000.

sections.label: Silver Support Scheme payments
sections.summary: The Silver Support income threshold rises from $1,800 to $2,300 and quarterly payments increase by 20%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Silver Support Scheme provides quarterly payments to seniors who had low incomes during their working years and have less family support.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will raise the qualifying per capita household income threshold for Silver Support from $1,800 to $2,300, and increase the quarterly payments by 20%, to keep pace with inflation.

sections.label: Majulah Package beneficiaries and cost
sections.summary: The Majulah Package will benefit about 1.6 million Singaporeans at a lifetime cost of $8.2 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In all, the Majulah Package will benefit about 1.6 million Singaporeans, at a total lifetime cost of $8.2 billion.

sections.label: MOH annual budget growth
sections.summary: The Ministry of Health's annual budget has tripled within a decade.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Health (MOH)’s annual budget has tripled within a decade.

sections.label: GST increase pre-funding healthcare
sections.summary: The GST increase pre-funds rising healthcare expenditure now rather than in the future.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The GST increase was meant for this purpose.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Essentially, we are pre-funding the rising healthcare expenditure by increasing GST now, instead of waiting to do so in the future.

sections.label: Healthier SG enrolment numbers
sections.summary: More than 700,000 Singapore residents have enrolled in Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: More than 700,000 Singapore residents have enrolled in Healthier SG.

sections.label: MediSave Bonus for adult Singaporeans
sections.summary: All adult Singaporeans aged 21 to 50 get a one-time MediSave Bonus of up to $300.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We want to ensure that all Singaporeans, including the self-employed and those not working, are able to build up their medical savings in anticipation of these rising costs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will therefore provide all adult Singaporeans aged 21 to 50 a one-time MediSave Bonus of up to $300.

sections.label: Age Well SG funding
sections.summary: Age Well SG is a new national programme for seniors, with $3.5 billion set aside over the next decade.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is why we have Age Well SG – it is a new national programme to support seniors to age actively, stay socially connected, and be cared for within their own communities.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will set aside $3.5 billion for Age Well SG initiatives over the next decade.

sections.label: LifeSG credits for NSmen
sections.summary: All past and present national servicemen receive $200 in LifeSG credits, costing $240 million and benefiting 1.2 million NSmen.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We owe a huge debt to our NSmen, who have served faithfully and made immeasurable sacrifices for our peace and security.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will therefore provide $200 in the form of LifeSG credits to all past and present national servicemen, including those enlisting this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It is a small gesture, but when you add it all up, it will cost us $240 million and benefit 1.2 million NSmen.

sections.label: National Cybersecurity Command Centre
sections.summary: A new National Cybersecurity Command Centre will be established at the Punggol Digital District to coordinate cyber defence operations.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We established the Digital and Intelligence Service in the SAF.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will establish a new National Cybersecurity Command Centre at the Punggol Digital District to better coordinate cyber defence operations, improve collaboration with industry and academia, and spur innovation in cybersecurity.

sections.label: Natural gas supply and second LNG terminal
sections.summary: Natural gas comes via pipelines from Indonesia and Malaysia and as LNG, and a second LNG terminal is planned for growing electricity needs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our natural gas supplies come through pipelines from Indonesia and Malaysia, and in the form of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from a range of sources.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are now planning to build a second LNG terminal to meet our growing electricity needs.

sections.label: Future Energy Fund with $5 billion
sections.summary: A Future Energy Fund will be set up with an initial $5 billion injection, as such work cannot be done by the private sector alone.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: They cannot be done by the private sector alone and will likely need some catalytic funding from the Government.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will therefore set up a Future Energy Fund with an initial injection of $5 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This will give us the confidence to invest in good time, put us in a better position to move quickly on critical infrastructure, and enhance our security in clean energy.

sections.label: Charities Capability Fund Collaboration Grant extension
sections.summary: The Charities Capability Fund Collaboration Grant will be extended for three years till end-FY2026 to encourage charities to work together.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In the same spirit, we want to encourage charities to work together to uplift each other and better meet the needs of beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will do so by extending the Charities Capability Fund Collaboration Grant for three years till end-FY2026.

sections.label: Overseas Humanitarian Assistance Tax Deduction Scheme
sections.summary: An Overseas Humanitarian Assistance Tax Deduction Scheme will give 100% tax deductions for cash donations to overseas emergency humanitarian assistance through designated charities.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To encourage Singaporeans to support those in need overseas, I will introduce an Overseas Humanitarian Assistance Tax Deduction Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This will provide 100% tax deductions for cash donations made towards overseas emergency humanitarian assistance causes through designated charities.

sections.label: Funding for Our SG Arts Plan
sections.summary: The National Arts Council has refreshed Our SG Arts Plan, and $100 million will be invested over the next four years to support it.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The National Arts Council (NAC) has refreshed Our SG Arts Plan to drive transformation efforts in the arts sector.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will support this plan by investing $100 million over the next four years.

sections.label: One Team Singapore Fund top-up and extension
sections.summary: A $20 million top-up will be provided for the One Team Singapore Fund, which gives dollar-for-dollar matching for donations to Team Singapore athletes, and it will be extended till end-FY2027.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We also have the One Team Singapore Fund, which provides dollar-for-dollar matching for donations towards Team Singapore athletes.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will provide a $20 million top-up for the One Team Singapore Fund and extend it till end-FY2027.

sections.label: Personal Income Tax Rebate
sections.summary: A 50% Personal Income Tax Rebate is provided for the Year of Assessment 2024 due to cost of living concerns.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: These moves have put us on a stronger fiscal footing for the next decade, while ensuring that our overall system of public finances remains fair and progressive.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This year, in light of concerns over cost of living, I will provide a Personal Income Tax Rebate of 50% for the Year of Assessment 2024.

sections.label: Dependant-related reliefs income threshold
sections.summary: From the Year of Assessment 2025, the annual income threshold for dependant-related reliefs rises from $4,000 to $8,000.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have received feedback from members of public, tax practitioners, as well as Labour Members of Parliament, to consider increasing the dependant income threshold in view of rising cost of living and wage levels.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, with effect from the Year of Assessment 2025, I will increase the annual income threshold for dependant-related reliefs from $4,000 to $8,000.

sections.label: Owner-occupier Property Tax AV bands
sections.summary: From 1 January 2025, all owner-occupier residential Property Tax AV bands are raised, with the lower threshold going from $8,000 to $12,000 and the highest from over $100,000 to over $140,000.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In light of these market trends, I will raise all the AV bands of the owner-occupier residential Property Tax rates with effect from 1 January 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Currently, Property Tax is charged on the bands of AV from $8,000 to over $100,000.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will raise the lower threshold from $8,000 to $12,000 and the highest band from over $100,000 to over $140,000, and corresponding adjustments will be made to the bands in between.

sections.label: Concession for right-sizing seniors
sections.summary: The concession is extended to single Singapore Citizens aged 55 and above who wish to right-size.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To better support seniors who wish to right-size, I will extend the concession to single Singapore Citizens aged 55 and above.

sections.label: ABSD clawback rate
sections.summary: The ABSD clawback rate is lowered if developers sell at least 90% of each development within the prescribed sale timeline.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: They are then subject to a full clawback of the ABSD.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will lower the ABSD clawback rate, should developers sell at least 90% of each development within the prescribed sale timeline.

sections.label: IIR and DTT for MNEs
sections.summary: The IIR and DTT take effect for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2025 for large MNE groups with global revenue of at least €750 million annually.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The IIR and the DTT will take effect for businesses’ financial years starting on or after 1 January 2025 and will apply to large MNE groups with global revenue of at least €750 million annually.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: There is another component of Pillar 2: the Undertaxed Profits Rule.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is effectively a backstop, as it will allow Singapore to collect a share of the top-up tax on any MNE with operations here, if any portion of its income overseas has not been subject to the minimum tax.

sections.label: No expected net revenue gains
sections.summary: The speaker does not expect the new moves to generate net revenue gains for Singapore on a sustained basis.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Overall, given the significant spending required to stay competitive, at this point, I do not expect the new moves to generate net revenue gains for Singapore on a sustained basis.

sections.label: Forward Singapore spending projections
sections.summary: About $5 billion will be spent on Forward Singapore policy moves in FY2024, close to $40 billion by the decade's end, with spending rising to around 20% of GDP by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I have just introduced some of these measures in this year’s Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will spend around $5 billion on Forward Singapore policy moves in FY2024 and close to $40 billion in total by the end of this decade.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In our projections, MOF had assessed that Government spending will increase to around 20% of GDP by 2030.

sections.label: FY2023 deficit and FY2024 surplus
sections.summary: FY2023 is expected to end with a $3.6 billion deficit, and FY2024 budgets a small surplus of $0.8 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Accounting for both our revenue upside and higher spending, we expect to end FY2023 with a deficit of $3.6 billion, or 0.5% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For FY2024, we are budgeting a small surplus of $0.8 billion, or 0.1% of GDP, which is essentially a balanced fiscal position.

sections.label: Equipping Singaporeans and social compact
sections.summary: The passage states plans to equip everyone, strengthen risk pooling and social support, and fortify resilience, citing a healthy fiscal position, trust, unity and a strong social compact.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will equip everyone to realise their potential and ensure that everyone benefits from our nation’s progress.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will strengthen our system of risk pooling and social support, so that Singaporeans can be better assured through every life stage, and better equipped to bounce back from every setback.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will fortify our resilience, solidarity and unity, so that we remain strong and effective against any challenges or threats.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Many find it hard to implement bold and long-term plans.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But we can make it happen in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are able to do so because: (a) our fiscal position is healthy and sustainable; (b) our Government has the trust of Singaporeans; (c) our people are united, and (d) our social compact is strong.

sections.label: Cherishing Singapore's strengths
sections.summary: The passage calls for cherishing, treasuring and harnessing these strengths to remain a shining red dot in a troubled world.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Let us cherish it, treasure it and harness these strengths to remain a shining red dot in a troubled world.

sections.label: Budget debate adjourned
sections.summary: The question seeks Parliament's approval of the Government's financial policy for 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025, and the debate now stands adjourned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Question is, "That Parliament approves the financial policy of the Government for the Financial Year 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025." In accordance with paragraph (1) of Standing Order No 89, the debate now stands adjourned.
